why.headline: Four reasons this isn't your usual supplier pitch.
why.r1.title: You know where it comes from
why.r1.body: Every batch is traceable to a named Japanese farm — not a blending facility, not a trading house. You get origin, region, harvest season, and flush. Your invoice says exactly what's inside your tin.
why.r2.title: You get real documentation
why.r2.body: Certificate of Origin, phytosanitary clearance, commercial invoice with HS codes, Portuguese-language labelling. No "trust me" — just paperwork that satisfies any inspection.
why.r3.title: The price makes your margin work
why.r3.body: We sell at import-direct pricing because that's exactly what it is. No layers. You buy closer to the farm than any European wholesaler allows — and your per-cup cost proves it.
why.r4.title: We only sell what's in season
why.r4.body: We don't stockpile. When a harvest arrives, we offer it. When it's gone, we wait. You'll never receive last year's tea repackaged as this year's — because we don't carry it.
japan.headline: Why Japan. Why this way.
japan.shinrai.title: Trust is earned, not claimed
japan.shinrai.body: In Japanese business, shinrai (信頼) — trust — isn't built on marketing. It's built on consistency, traceability, and keeping your word. Every batch we sell is an act of shinrai: verifiable, documented, and backed by a named farm.
japan.genzen.title: A curated standard
japan.genzen.body: We don't list hundreds of SKUs. We work with a small number of farms and select only what meets our threshold — in colour, aroma, taste, and grind. If a harvest doesn't pass, we don't sell it. That's why our range is tight: because we'd rather have seven excellent tiers than seventy average ones.
japan.chokusetsu.title: Direct means direct
japan.chokusetsu.body: We are not a distributor pretending to be close to the source. We import directly from Japanese farms via seasonal contracts. There is no European middleman. No blending house. No repackager. The tea that reaches your café left Japan in the same form — with the same traceability — as when it was packed at the farm.

serve.wellness.pain: "I need a clean-label matcha I can actually trust."
serve.wellness.body: Single-origin, no additives, no blending. Our matcha and hojicha are exactly what the label says — nothing else. Perfect for smoothie bars, health food stores, and plant-based menus that need to back up their claims.

compliance.headline: Everything your inspector wants to see.
compliance.sub: We don't just sell tea — we deliver it with every document required under EU and Portuguese food safety law.

compliance.1.body: Issued per batch by the Japanese Chamber of Commerce, confirming the tea's origin and production region. Required for EU import clearance.
compliance.2.title: Batch Traceability
compliance.2.body: Each shipment carries harvest date, flush, farm name, and region. Your customers can ask — and you'll have the answer.
compliance.3.title: Portuguese-Language Labels

faq.q1.q: What's the difference between Japanese and Chinese matcha?
faq.q1.a: Japanese matcha is shade-grown for 20–30 days before harvest using tencha leaves, then stone-ground. Chinese matcha is typically sun-grown, industrially milled, and often colour-corrected with E141 dye. The difference is visible in the cup — and obvious in milk.
faq.q2.q: What is a Batch ID and why does my café need one?
faq.q2.a: Every batch Nokari ships carries a unique ID linked to a specific farm, harvest season, and full documentation set. If a customer asks where it's from — you can show them. If a regulator asks — same answer.
faq.q3.q: Why does your matcha change from batch to batch?
faq.q3.a: Because we select the best farm each season rather than locking in one supplier year-round. Think natural wine — specific producer, specific harvest. The quality is always higher than a fixed "consistent average" product.
faq.q4.q: How do I know the matcha hasn't oxidised in transit?
faq.q4.a: Colour is the first indicator. Vibrant jade green means fresh. Olive or yellowish means oxidised. We ship in hermetically sealed, nitrogen-flushed packaging with the production date clearly marked on every unit.
faq.q5.q: What is your minimum order quantity?
faq.q5.a: From 500g for a first trial. From 1kg for a standard order. From 5kg for wholesale pricing.
faq.q6.q: Do you provide a matcha latte SOP?
faq.q6.a: Yes. Every order includes a preparation card with exact ratios, water temperature, sifting technique, and the most common barista mistakes — solved.
faq.q7.q: Our baristas complain about clumping. Is that a powder problem?
faq.q7.a: Usually it's technique or water temperature, not the powder. Our SOP card resolves 95% of these cases. If it doesn't — message us and we'll work through it together.
faq.q8.q: What does one matcha latte serving cost with your product?
faq.q8.a: At standard pricing with a 3g dose — €0.47 per cup. At a menu price of €5–6, that's over 90% margin.
faq.q9.q: How fast do you deliver within Portugal?
faq.q9.a: 24–48 hours after order confirmation. Regular clients get priority allocation when batch quantities are limited.
faq.q10.q: Can I try a sample before committing to a first order?
faq.q10.a: Yes. The Nokari sample kit is €25 and includes both matcha and hojicha. The full amount is credited against your first order.
faq.q11.q: Do you provide certificates of origin?
faq.q11.a: Yes. Certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, and product specification sheet are included with every batch.
faq.q12.q: Who handles Portuguese-language labelling — you or us?
faq.q12.a: We do. Every product ships with labelling compliant with ASAE requirements and Portuguese food law. Nothing extra on your end.
faq.q13.a: The current batch is pesticide-free with full documentation, but does not carry an organic certificate. If organic certification is a hard requirement for your venue — reach out and we'll discuss options for the next batch.
faq.q14.q: You change farms every season — isn't that unstable?
faq.q14.a: It's the opposite. We're not locked into one producer — we choose whoever is at their quality peak right now. If a farm had a weak harvest, we don't take it. You always get the best available product, not a "reliably average" one.
faq.q15.q: What if I order and the product doesn't work for us?
faq.q15.a: Contact us within 7 days. We'll either replace the batch or find a solution. A B2B partnership isn't a one-time transaction.
faq.q16.q: Do you only work with Portugal?
faq.q16.a: Portugal is the current focus. Spain is next. If you're based in Spain and want to be first in — get in touch and we'll discuss terms.
